measurement.mode: static Vite client bundle graph — no browser, no network, no rendering
measurement.browser: not applicable. The gate never launches a browser; it reads the chunk graph the Vite build emits (dist/client/bundle-graph.json) and sums, per route, the client entry chunk, the static-import closure of the route's own chunk, and the chunks of its layout ancestors (a nested route renders its parent layouts). Browser-dependent behaviour is out of scope by design — see Issue #384 (Lighthouse measurement) and #385 (score gate).
measurement.network: not applicable. Budgeted numbers are RAW on-disk bytes of the files a browser must fetch before the route is interactive. gzip -9 figures are printed for reference only and are never budgeted, because a CDN's compression settings are not part of this measurement.
measurement.cpu: not time-based. The measurement is byte arithmetic over a build artefact, so it is deterministic on any machine and independent of runner speed. Only the wall-clock cost of `pnpm run build` that produces the artefact is runner-dependent.
measurement.source_sha: the commit the run is executed at, printed as `git rev-parse HEAD`. In CI the client build and this check run in the same job against the same SHA, so a red run always names the exact tree that was measured; locally, rebuild before rerunning if the tree changed. The gate also warns (it does not fail) when the graph's recorded client assets no longer exist under its own out_dir, which is what a stale or foreign `dist/client/bundle-graph.json` looks like.
measurement.reproduce_locally: pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check
measurement.reproduce_in_ci: the `validate` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `pnpm run validate:integration`, which runs this check immediately after `pnpm run build:production`.

headroom_policy: This field is the derivation history in order; only the final Issue #495 paragraph describes the caps currently in this file, and the earlier SHAs name the build each earlier revision was measured at, not the current one. Every JS cap is the measured `initial_js_bytes` plus at least 0.35% headroom, rounded up to the next multiple of 5,000 bytes: `ceil(measured * 1.0035 / 5000) * 5000`. The current caps were re-derived from one `pnpm run build` of this branch measured at `2793bd80` (the PR head at the time of the measurement). `origin/release-0-7-0` stood at `38c28818` then, and its newer commits touch only `src/http/**` and `src/server.ts` — server-side code that is not part of the client bundle graph — so the measurement describes the tree CI builds as well. Measured initial JS on that build ranged from 1,587,977 B (`/admin`) to 1,637,331 B (`/design-system`), and the slack the formula leaves is +0.39% (`/admin/keys`) to +0.64% (`/admin/emoji-catalog`). The initial CSS measured 42,397 B, inside the shared 45,000 B cap. CSS is budgeted on one shared cap rather than per route: the initial stylesheet is a single asset every route pulls in, so a per-route CSS cap would be 16 copies of the same number. That shared CSS cap was re-derived after the base merged #485 (`src/styles.css` font first-paint work), which moved the measured initial CSS from 38,681 B to 40,028 B; the cap is 45,000 B for the same reason JS caps are rounded to 5,000 B boundaries (one boundary of headroom on a number that is already inside it). Measured bytes are read back from the files Rollup emitted (`writeBundle` in `vite.config.ts` → `scripts/_client-bundle-graph.mjs`), so a cap is compared against the exact bytes a browser downloads — including the preload marker and dependency map that Vite injects after an ordinary user plugin's `generateBundle` runs. Because the entry shell is shared, ~1.5 MiB of every admin route, a base merge that adds a few hundred bytes to the shell re-derives several route caps at once; that is why a release merge turns this gate red until the caps are re-measured with `pnpm run build && pnpm run bundle:budget:check`. It is the gate doing its job, not a flaky test. The caps are intentionally tight: the entry chunk alone is ~1.5 MiB because `emoji-picker-react` is statically imported (see the Vite chunk warning in the build log), so a per-route cap is the only place a regression of that kind is visible today. Reducing the shell is a separate change with its own Issue; this gate only makes the number visible and stops it from moving silently. Note that raising a cap is not machine-checked — only an `exception` is — so a cap change is expected to carry its measurement and rationale in the PR diff. Issue #496 re-derived every route cap twice: the published data-lifecycle registry (`src/privacy/data-lifecycle.ts`) ships to the client through the home footer, so the shared entry shell grew by 10.7 KiB of static bilingual policy text, and the review round grew it a little further (the analytics sentence now names the first-page_view limit, and the admin-auth sentence names the token-gated accept page). `/admin` measured 1,587,977 B, and the five routes whose measured bytes crossed their previous cap boundary (`/admin/`, `/admin/emoji-catalog`, `/admin/invitations/accept`, `/contact`, `/portfolio/$slug`) moved up by one 5,000 B step each; the other eleven caps did not move. The shared CSS cap (measured 42,397 B) and the Tool iframe aggregate were not touched. A future PR that renders this notice without shipping it — a server-only projection — should re-derive the caps downward again. A JS cap is the measured `initial_js_bytes` plus at least 0.35% headroom, rounded up to the next multiple of 5,000 bytes: `ceil(measured * 1.0035 / 5000) * 5000`. A cap records the measurement it was derived from, so a route whose measurement moved after the cap was set can carry a cap that is no longer the formula output — those are named explicitly below and are left alone on purpose, because raising a cap that is not red is a decision, not a measurement. The caps were last re-derived from one `pnpm run build` of this branch with `origin/release-0-7-0` at `b25b0459` merged in, so the numbers describe the tree this PR merges into — not the tree the first draft was written against. Issue #495 re-derived sixteen JS caps from one `pnpm run build` of this branch measured at `e0cbbc31` (the merge commit that brought `origin/release-0-7-0` in), with the branch's final review fixes applied on top: the consent gate, its panel and the shared consent rules are statically reachable from `src/routes/__root.tsx`, so they add bytes to every route shell. Measured initial JS was / 1,630,831 B, /about 1,620,575 B, /admin 1,600,129 B, /admin/ 1,603,522 B, /admin/emoji-catalog 1,607,016 B, /admin/images 1,610,215 B, /admin/invitations 1,609,226 B, /admin/invitations/accept 1,607,943 B, /admin/keys 1,610,969 B, /admin/login 1,605,505 B, /contact 1,612,530 B, /design-system 1,649,483 B, /portfolio/ 1,640,007 B, /portfolio/$slug 1,642,097 B, /tools/ 1,604,611 B, /tools/$slug 1,607,663 B. The same formula was applied to each route; every resulting cap equals the cap already in this file, so this reconcile changed the recorded measurement and its provenance, not a cap. The initial CSS measured 43,355 B, still inside the shared 45,000 B cap. Growth is the cost of a consent gate that renders on the client only; shrinking the entry shell is a separate change with its own Issue. Issue #620 re-derived the caps twice, and both measurements are kept here. The ticket branch measured them on its own tree at `0467ea67` — the numbers in the paragraph above — and the release merge then brought in the analytics consent gate (Issue #495) and the other `release-0-7-0` commits, so the caps were measured again on the merged tree: one `pnpm run build` of `origin/release-0-7-0` merged into the ticket branch measured initial JS 1,647,052 B (`/admin`) through 1,696,665 B (`/design-system`), `/keyboard` 1,683,369 B, `/portfolio/` 1,687,271 B, and an initial CSS of 46,085 B, still inside the shared 50,000 B cap. tool_iframe.reason: Each Tool is an independent Vite build loaded inside a sandboxed iframe from /tools/<slug>/app/, so its bytes are never part of a host route's first paint. Capping it separately keeps one heavy Tool from being hidden by the host route budget and stops a Tool from inflating the host measurement. The cap is the observed `prototype` bundle (1,502,757 B JS / 8,415 B CSS) plus headroom; the Tool's own repository owns any reduction.
